definition_en: a medical instrument with a chest piece and earpieces, used to listen to the sounds of the heart and lungs
core_image: 挂在颈上的小管子，把胸腔里的心跳声送到耳边
scene: 诊室里，医生把听诊器贴在病人胸口，安静地听着。The doctor pressed the stethoscope to the chest of the patient and listened for a heartbeat.
sceneCN: 这里 stethoscope 是「听诊器」（第 1 个义项：用来听心音与呼吸音的器械）；句意：诊室里，医生把听诊器贴在病人胸口，听心跳的声音。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「听诊器的；用听诊器听到的」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「听诊；用听诊器检查」

senses.title: A listening instrument
senses.definition: a medical tool with a chest piece and earpieces, used to listen to the heart and lungs
senses.definitionCN: 由胸件与耳塞组成、用来听心音与呼吸音的医疗器械
senses.example: The doctor used a stethoscope to check the lungs of the patient.
senses.exampleCN: 医生用听诊器检查病人的肺部。
senses.why: Greek stethos means chest and skopein means to look, so the name describes an instrument for examining the chest.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 stethos 意为「胸」，skopein 意为「看」，名字本指检查胸部的器具，实际却用来听胸内的声音。

senses.title: A sign of the medical calling
senses.definition: the instrument as a familiar emblem of doctors and clinical care
senses.definitionCN: 作为医生与临床照护的常见象征的听诊器
senses.example: In films, a stethoscope around the neck signals the doctor.
senses.exampleCN: 在电影里，脖子上挂着听诊器就表示此人是医生。
senses.why: Because it hangs on the neck and appears in every examination, the object itself became a visual badge of the profession.
senses.whyCN: 因为它常挂在颈上、出现在每次检查中，这件器物本身就成了这一职业的视觉徽章。

senses.title: A device for the unborn child
senses.definition: a special stethoscope used to listen to the heartbeat of an unborn baby
senses.definitionCN: 用来听胎儿心跳的特殊听诊器
senses.example: The midwife reached for the fetal stethoscope.
senses.exampleCN: 助产士伸手去拿胎心听诊器。
senses.why: The same listening principle is narrowed to one small, fast heartbeat before birth.
senses.whyCN: 同样的听音原理被缩小到出生前那颗细小而快速的心跳上。

senses.title: An amplified listening tool
senses.definition: an electronic version that amplifies body sounds for clearer hearing
senses.definitionCN: 放大体内声音以便听得更清楚的电子版本
senses.example: An electronic stethoscope can make faint murmurs audible.
senses.exampleCN: 电子听诊器能让微弱的心杂音变得听得见。
senses.why: Once the chest sound is turned into a signal, it can be amplified and shared, which is the modern extension of the old tube.
senses.whyCN: 一旦胸部的声音被转成信号，就能放大与共享，这是旧式导管在现代的延伸。

intro.en: Stethoscope was coined in French from Greek stethos, chest, and skopein, to look at.
intro.cn: stethoscope 由法语据希腊语 stethos（胸）与 skopein（看、检查）造出。

items.en: Stethos means chest, the part of the body being examined.
items.cn: stethos 意为「胸」，即被检查的部位。

items.en: Skopein means to look at or examine.
Rene Laennec coins stethoscope for his new listening tube.
items.cn: 法国医生勒内克为他的听音管造出 stethoscope 一词。

items.en: New Latin stethoscopium gives the word a classical shape.
items.cn: 新拉丁语 stethoscopium 使这个词获得古典外形。

items.en: English adopts stethoscope as the name of the instrument.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪采用 stethoscope 作为该器械的名称。

items.en: Modern forms add electronic and fetal stethoscopes.
items.cn: 现代英语又衍生出电子听诊器与胎心听诊器。

note.en: Stethoscope belongs to the Greek family of viewing instruments and to the near field of listening tools.
note.cn: stethoscope 属于希腊语「观察器具」词族，也靠近「听诊工具」这一义场。

entries.definition: relating to a stethoscope or to auscultation
an instrument for looking into the ear
entries.definitionCN: 耳镜；与 stethoscope 共享 -scope 词尾

entries.definition: the act of listening to sounds inside the body
entries.definitionCN: 听诊；听体内声音的行为

entries.definition: a device that detects blood flow by sound
entries.definitionCN: 多普勒仪；用声音探测血流的装置

entries.definition: the part worn in the ear
entries.definitionCN: 耳塞；听诊器戴在耳中的部件

normalIntro.en: Stethoscope joins two Greek pieces, chest and looking, into an instrument that examines the chest by sound.
normalIntro.cn: stethoscope 由两个希腊语成分拼成：胸与看，一件用声音检查胸部的器具。

normal.en: Break the word into stetho, chest, and scope, look.
normal.cn: 拆成 stetho（胸）与 scope（看），一看就懂。

normal.en: A stethoscope has a chest piece and two earpieces.
normal.cn: 听诊器有一个胸件和两个耳塞。

normal.en: Doctors hang a stethoscope around the neck.
normal.cn: 医生把听诊器挂在脖子上。

normal.en: An electronic stethoscope amplifies faint sounds.
normal.cn: 电子听诊器能放大微弱的声音。

normal.en: Compare stethoscopy, the act of listening with this tool.
normal.cn: 对比 stethoscopy，指用这件工具听诊的行为。

abstract.en: Picture a small tube carrying the drum of a heartbeat to your ear.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细管把心跳的鼓点送到耳边。

abstract.en: See the tubing hanging on a white coat like a badge.
abstract.cn: 想象管子挂在白大褂上，像一枚徽章。

abstract.en: Think of a tiny heartbeat heard through a horn before birth.
abstract.cn: 想象出生前，用一只小喇叭听见细微的心跳。

examples.en: The doctor listened to the chest of the child with a stethoscope.
examples.cn: 医生用听诊器听了孩子的胸部。

examples.en: She cleaned the stethoscope before the next patient.
examples.cn: 她在看下一位病人前清洁了听诊器。

examples.en: Modern stethoscopes can record heart sounds electronically.
examples.cn: 现代听诊器可以用电子方式记录心音。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯泰思可」——联想「思」考时把「听」筒贴在胸口；这只是谐音拆字联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 stethos（胸） + skopein（看、检查）→ 法语 stéthoscope → 英语 stethoscope，字面是「看胸的器具」，实用功能却是听胸内的声音。

sensesIntro.en: Stethoscope names the instrument first, then the professional emblem, the fetal version, and the electronic amplifier.
sensesIntro.cn: stethoscope 先指这件器械，再指医生身份的象征，又指胎心版本与电子放大器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin tube that brings the sound of the chest to the ear.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细管把胸腔的声音送到耳边。

branches.en: The plain instrument is the first sense.
branches.cn: 普通器械是第一个义项。

branches.en: The hanging tube becomes a badge of the profession.
branches.cn: 挂着的管子成为职业徽章。

branches.en: A small version serves the unborn child.
branches.cn: 小型版本服务于未出生的孩子。

branches.en: Electronics extend the old tube into an amplifier.
branches.cn: 电子技术把旧导管延伸为放大器。

branches.en: Both the plain and the electronic forms share one listening job.
branches.cn: 普通版与电子版承担同一种听音任务。

intro.en: Stethoscope is built from two Greek roots and a suffix, with English adjectives and nouns around it.
intro.cn: stethoscope 由两个希腊词根加一个词尾构成，英语围绕它还有形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The word was Latinized as stethoscopium in medical Latin, from Greek stethos and skopein.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词在医学拉丁语中写作 stethoscopium，源自希腊语 stethos 与 skopein。

items.exampleCN: 词尾 -scope 也出现在 otoscope 中。

latinEntries.meaning: a listening instrument for the chest

definition_en: a tube with a needle or nozzle, used to inject or withdraw fluids
core_image: 推杆在细管里缓缓前推，药液从针尖流出
scene: 护士把针头装到注射器上，抽好了药液。The nurse fitted a needle to the syringe and drew up the medicine.
sceneCN: 这里 syringe 是「注射器」（第 1 个义项：带针头用来注药或抽液的器械）；句意：护士给注射器装上针头，抽好了药液。

derivatives.zh: 与希腊语「管」词根同源，加形容词后缀构成，义为「鸣管的；与鸟类鸣管有关的」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「用注射器灌洗；冲洗」
由希腊语「管」词根加「脊髓」构成，义为「脊髓空洞症」

senses.title: A needle instrument for injecting
senses.definition: a small tube with a plunger and a needle, used to push medicine into the body
senses.definitionCN: 带推杆和针头、把药液推入体内的小管
senses.example: The nurse filled the syringe with painkiller.
senses.exampleCN: 护士把止痛药吸进注射器。
senses.why: Greek syrinx means a pipe, and the first syringes were simple tubes that pushed liquid.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 syrinx 意为「管」，最早的注射器就是推液体的简单管子。

senses.title: A tool for taking fluid out
senses.definition: a device used to draw blood or fluid out of the body
senses.definitionCN: 把血液或体液从体内抽出的器具
senses.example: A syringe drew blood from the arm of the donor.
senses.exampleCN: 一支注射器从献血者的手臂上抽了血。
senses.why: The same plunger works both ways, so pulling back turns the injector into an extractor.
senses.whyCN: 同一个推杆可以双向工作，往回拉就把注药器变成了抽液器。

senses.title: A bulb for washing a cavity
senses.definition: a rubber bulb with a nozzle, used to flush the ear or a wound
senses.definitionCN: 带喷嘴的橡胶球，用来冲洗耳朵或伤口
senses.example: The ear was cleaned with a soft bulb syringe.
senses.exampleCN: 耳朵用柔软的球式灌洗器清洗过。
senses.why: Without a needle the tube becomes a gentle washer, aimed at cleaning rather than piercing.
senses.whyCN: 去掉针头后，管子就成了温和的冲洗器，用来清洁而不是穿刺。

senses.title: A tube for spraying liquid
senses.definition: an old or industrial tube that squirts liquid in a stream
senses.definitionCN: 古代或工业上用来把液体喷成一股的管子
senses.example: An old garden syringe sprayed water over the plants.
senses.exampleCN: 一只旧的园艺喷管把水喷在植物上。
senses.why: The pipe root also covers any tube that shoots liquid, not only medical ones.
senses.whyCN: 「管」这个词根也涵盖任何喷射液体的管子，并不限于医用。

intro.en: Syringe goes back through Latin syrinx to Greek syrinx, a pipe or tube.
intro.cn: syringe 经拉丁语 syrinx 上溯至希腊语 syrinx，意为「管」。

items.en: Syrinx means a pipe, a tube, or a pan flute.
items.cn: syrinx 意为管、导管，也指排箫。

items.en: Latin keeps syrinx for a tube or a fistula.
items.cn: 拉丁语 syrinx 指管或瘘管。

items.en: Syringe appears in English for a medical tube.
items.cn: 中古英语 syringe 指医用管子。

items.en: The spelling settles as syringe in medical writing.
items.cn: 在医学文献中拼写固定为 syringe。

items.en: Modern English adds disposable and hypodermic syringes.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了一次性注射器与皮下注射器。

note.en: Syringe shares the Greek pipe image with syrinx and its small English family, and sits near the vocabulary of injection.
note.cn: syringe 与 syrinx 及其英语小词族共享希腊语「管」的意象，也靠近注射相关的词汇。

entries.definition: a pipe or the voice organ of birds
relating to the syrinx of birds
entries.definitionCN: 鸣管的；与鸟类鸣管有关的

entries.definition: the act of flushing with a syringe
the sharp part that enters the body
entries.definitionCN: 针头；刺入体内的尖锐部件

entries.definition: a device that pushes fluid in
entries.definitionCN: 注射装置；把液体推入的器具

entries.definition: a small bottle that holds the medicine

normalIntro.en: Syringe is a Greek pipe word, so the tube shape is the whole memory.
normalIntro.cn: syringe 是希腊语「管」一系的词，记住管形就记住了它。

normal.en: Syringe and syrinx share the pipe image.
normal.cn: syringe 与 syrinx 共享「管」的意象。

normal.en: A syringe has a barrel, a plunger, and a needle.
normal.cn: 注射器有管身、推杆和针头。

normal.en: A hypodermic syringe goes under the skin.
normal.cn: 皮下注射器把药送到皮肤下面。

normal.en: A disposable syringe is used once and thrown away.
normal.cn: 一次性注射器用一次就丢弃。

normal.en: A syringe pump pushes medicine slowly and steadily.
normal.cn: 注射泵缓慢而稳定地推药。

abstract.en: Watch the plunger move down and the liquid leave the needle.
abstract.cn: 想象推杆下压，药液从针尖离开。

abstract.en: See the same plunger pull back and fill the barrel with blood.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个推杆回拉，管身里吸满了血。

abstract.en: Picture a soft bulb squirting water into a small ear.
abstract.cn: 想象一只软球把水喷进小小的耳朵。

examples.en: The nurse filled the syringe and gave the injection.
examples.cn: 护士把药吸进注射器并打了针。

examples.en: Blood was drawn with a sterile syringe.
examples.cn: 用一支无菌注射器抽了血。

examples.en: Disposable syringes reduce the risk of infection.
examples.cn: 一次性注射器降低了感染风险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟琳奇」——联想「吸」管里「灵」巧一推，药就进去了；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 syrinx（管、排箫）→ 拉丁语 syrinx（管、瘘管）→ 中古英语 syringe，核心义「细管」，引申为注药与抽液的器械。

sensesIntro.en: Syringe starts as a pipe-shaped injector, then a suction tool, a washing bulb, and a spraying tube.
sensesIntro.cn: syringe 先指管状注药器，再指抽液工具、灌洗球与喷液管。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow tube with a plunger moving liquid in or out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细管配推杆，把液体推进或抽出。

branches.en: The pipe becomes a needle injector.
branches.cn: 管子变成带针头的注药器。

branches.en: Pulling the plunger reverses the flow.
branches.cn: 回拉推杆就让液体反向流动。

branches.en: A bulb without a needle becomes a washer.
branches.cn: 去掉针头的球体变成冲洗器。

branches.en: Any tube that sprays liquid keeps the old pipe sense.
branches.cn: 任何喷射液体的管子都保留古老的「管」义。

branches.en: Medical and garden tubes share the same pipe shape.
branches.cn: 医用与园艺用的管子共享同一种管形。

intro.en: Syringe is a Greek pipe word, with a Latin and English family built on the same tube image.
intro.cn: syringe 是希腊语「管」一系的词，拉丁语与英语词族都建立在同一根管子的意象上。

latinIntro.en: Greek syrinx passed into Latin as syrinx, a tube or fistula, and then into English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 syrinx 进入拉丁语仍作 syrinx，指管或瘘管，随后进入英语。

items.example: Latin keeps syrinx for a tube.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留 syrinx 指管。

items.example: To syringe a wound is to wash it.
items.exampleCN: to syringe a wound 就是冲洗伤口。
前缀 hypo- 构成 hypodermic。

definition_en: an abnormal mass of tissue, or a swollen area
core_image: 皮肤下鼓起一个硬硬的小包，慢慢变大
scene: 体检时，医生在病人背上摸到一个肿块，安排了进一步检查。During the checkup, the doctor felt a tumor on the back of the patient and ordered further tests.
sceneCN: 这里 tumor 是「肿块、肿瘤」（第 1 个义项：组织异常增生形成的团块）；句意：体检时，医生在病人背上摸到一个肿块，安排了进一步检查。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「肿瘤的；肿胀的」
由本词加「产生」词根与形容词后缀构成，义为「致瘤的」
由本词加「发生」词根构成，义为「肿瘤发生」

senses.title: An abnormal mass of tissue
senses.definition: a lump of tissue that grows abnormally, whether harmless or dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 异常生长的一团组织，无论无害还是危险
senses.example: The scan found a small tumor near the kidney.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描在肾脏附近发现一个小肿瘤。
senses.why: Latin tumor simply meant a swelling, and any new lump kept that bodily image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tumor 本意就是「肿胀」，任何新长出的团块都延续了这个身体意象。

senses.title: A cancerous growth
senses.definition: a mass of cells that can invade nearby tissue and spread
senses.definitionCN: 能侵犯邻近组织并转移的细胞团块
senses.example: The biopsy confirmed that the tumor was malignant.
senses.exampleCN: 活检确认这个肿瘤是恶性的。
senses.why: When doctors needed a neutral word for a growth, the old swelling noun became the medical term.
senses.whyCN: 当医生需要一个中性的词来指增生时，这个古老的「肿胀」名词就成了医学术语。

senses.title: A harmless lump
senses.definition: a growth that stays in place and does not spread
senses.definitionCN: 留在原处、不会转移的增生
senses.example: A benign tumor usually needs no urgent surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 良性肿瘤通常不需要紧急手术。
senses.why: The same word covers harmless lumps, so benign is added to draw the line.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也涵盖无害的肿块，所以再加上 benign 来划清界线。

senses.title: A swelling of the body
senses.definition: an old or general sense of a swollen part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 身体某处肿起的古老或一般说法
senses.example: The old medical text spoke of a tumor of the leg.
senses.exampleCN: 那本古老的医学书提到腿部的一处肿胀。
senses.why: The oldest sense is plain swelling, before the word was narrowed to new growths.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意义就是单纯的肿胀，后来才缩小到指新生的团块。

intro.en: Tumor is Latin for a swelling, from tumere, to swell.
intro.cn: tumor 是拉丁语「肿胀」，来自 tumere（肿起）。

items.en: Tumere means to swell or be swollen.
Tumor names a swelling or a swollen place.
items.cn: tumor 指肿胀或肿起的部位。

items.en: Old French tumeur carries the medical sense.
items.cn: 古法语 tumeur 承载医学含义。

items.en: English writes tumour for a swelling or a mass.
items.cn: 英语写作 tumour，指肿胀或团块。

items.en: American spelling settles as tumor, and medicine narrows it to growths.
items.cn: 美式拼写固定为 tumor，医学把词义缩小到增生团块。

note.en: Tumor belongs to the Latin swelling family and sits near the medical words for growths.
note.cn: tumor 属于拉丁语「肿胀」词族，并与表示增生的医学词汇相邻。

entries.definition: a new abnormal growth of tissue
a swollen place on the body
a disease of uncontrolled cell growth
entries.definitionCN: 癌症；细胞失控生长的疾病

normalIntro.en: Tumor is the Latin word for a swelling, so the word is a lump you can almost feel.
normalIntro.cn: tumor 就是拉丁语的「肿胀」，这个词本身就是能摸到的团块。

normal.en: Tumere, to swell, is the root behind tumor.
normal.cn: tumere（肿起）是 tumor 的词根。

normal.en: A benign tumor stays put; a malignant one spreads.
normal.cn: 良性肿瘤留在原处，恶性肿瘤会扩散。

normal.en: A brain tumor grows inside the skull.
Surgeons remove a tumor when they can.
normal.cn: 条件允许时，外科医生会切除肿瘤。

normal.en: Tumorous means full of or like a tumor.
normal.cn: tumorous 表示长有肿瘤或像肿瘤的。

abstract.en: Feel a hard pea under the skin that slowly becomes a marble.
abstract.cn: 想象皮下有一颗硬豌豆，慢慢长成弹珠。

abstract.en: See a small knot of cells sending out roots.
abstract.cn: 想象一小团细胞向外伸出根须。

abstract.en: Picture a lump that stays quietly in one place.
abstract.cn: 想象一个团块安静地待在一处。

examples.en: The scan showed a tumor in the left lung.
examples.cn: 扫描显示左肺有一个肿瘤。

examples.en: Benign tumors do not spread to other organs.
examples.cn: 良性肿瘤不会转移到其他器官。

examples.en: The surgeon removed the tumor successfully.
examples.cn: 外科医生成功切除了肿瘤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「突猛」——想象皮下「突」然鼓起一「猛」块；只是谐音联想，非词源。

root: 拉丁语 tumere（肿起）→ tumor（肿胀、肿块）→ 古法语 tumeur → 英语 tumor，核心义「肿起的团块」。

sensesIntro.en: Tumor starts as any swelling, then narrows to a new growth, splits into cancerous and harmless lumps, and keeps the old bodily sense.
sensesIntro.cn: tumor 先指任何肿胀，再缩小到新生团块，又分出恶性与良性两类，同时保留古老的「肿起」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump under the skin that slowly grows.
core.cn: 核心意象：皮下慢慢变大的团块。

branches.en: Any abnormal mass is the first sense.
branches.cn: 任何异常团块都是第一个义项。

branches.en: A spreading mass is the malignant sense.
branches.cn: 会转移的团块是恶性义。

branches.en: A fixed mass is the benign sense.
branches.cn: 固定不动的团块是良性义。

branches.en: Plain swelling is the oldest bodily sense.
branches.cn: 单纯的肿胀是最古老的身体义。

branches.en: Both the neutral lump and the cancerous growth share the mass image.
branches.cn: 中性团块与癌性增生共享同一个团块意象。

intro.en: Tumor is a Latin swelling noun, with English adjectives and a Greek suffix in its medical family.
intro.cn: tumor 是拉丁语表示肿胀的名词，医学词族里有英语形容词与希腊语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin tumere means to swell, and tumor means a swelling.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tumere 意为肿起，tumor 意为肿胀。

items.exampleCN: tumere 是表示肿起的动词。
tumor 是表示肿胀的名词。

items.example: Tumour is common in British writing.
items.exampleCN: tumour 常见于英式写作用法。
